nodes.label: Visual Brainstorming (Browser Displays, Terminal Commands)
nodes.rationale: Non-blocking architecture where the browser is an interactive display and the terminal stays the conversation channel; user clicks are recorded for the agent to read on its next turn.

nodes.label: .events File Feedback Architecture
nodes.rationale: Server writes user events (choice clicks) to a per-screen .events file (JSONL) that Claude reads on its next turn; cleared when a new screen is pushed. Replaces wait-for-feedback.sh and TaskOutput blocking.

nodes.label: Brainstorm Server (Express/WebSocket + file watching)
nodes.rationale: Node.js server serving newest HTML in a watched screen directory to the browser, wrapping fragments in a frame template, and handling WebSocket choice events. Evolved from Express/ws/chokidar to zero-dependency Node built-ins (http, crypto, fs, path).

nodes.label: Spec & Plan Document Review System
nodes.rationale: Adds spec document reviewer (brainstorming skill) and plan document reviewer (writing-plans skill) prompt templates with review loops dispatching general-purpose subagents via the Task tool.

nodes.label: Git Environment Detection (GIT_DIR vs GIT_COMMON)
nodes.rationale: Read-only detection comparing git rev-parse --git-dir and --git-common-dir to decide whether the agent is already in a linked worktree or on a detached HEAD (externally managed sandbox).

nodes.label: Brainstorming Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Shared skill hosting the spec reviewer loop and the visual-companion.md / brainstorm server scripts.

nodes.label: Writing Plans Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Shared skill hosting the plan review loop, checkbox task syntax, and the plan document header template.

nodes.label: Subagent-Driven Development Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Required execution method for these implementation plans; also a target of the worktree integration updates.

nodes.label: Executing Plans Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Inline-plan execution alternative used when subagents are unavailable.

nodes.label: Using Git Worktrees Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Rewritten to native-worktree-tool-first (Step 1a) with git fallback (Step 1b), Step 0 isolation detection, submodule guard, and sandbox fallback.

nodes.label: Finishing a Development Branch Skill (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Rewritten with environment detection before the options menu, detached-HEAD 3-option variant, and provenance-based cleanup (only removes .worktrees/ or superpowers global worktrees).

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
nodes.rationale: Used as the testing-skills-with-subagents framework: RED baseline then GREEN validation gate for the native worktree preference (EnterWorktree over git worktree add).

nodes.label: Code Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Role dispatched via Task tool to review completed work against its plan or requirements before issues cascade into more work.

nodes.label: Review Dimensions
nodes.rationale: What to check: plan alignment, code quality, architecture, testing, production readiness.

nodes.label: Severity Triage
nodes.rationale: Issues categorized as Critical (Must Fix), Important (Should Fix), Minor (Nice to Have); calibration says not everything is Critical.

nodes.label: Review Output Format
nodes.rationale: Reviewer returns Strengths, Issues (Critical/Important/Minor), Recommendations, Assessment with Ready to merge verdict.

nodes.label: Skill Invocation Rule
nodes.rationale: Invoke relevant skills BEFORE any response or action; even a 1% chance a skill might apply means invoke it. Skill tool invocation required before ANY response including clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Skill Priority Ordering
nodes.rationale: Process skills first (brainstorming, debugging) determine HOW; implementation skills second (frontend-design, mcp-builder) guide execution.

nodes.label: Rigid vs Flexible Skills
nodes.rationale: Rigid skills (TDD, debugging) follow exactly; flexible skills (patterns) adapt principles to context; the skill tells you which.

nodes.label: Instruction Priority Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: User instructions (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md) highest priority, then superpowers skills, then default system prompt.

nodes.label: Platform Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Skills use Claude Code tool names; non-CC platforms map tool equivalents via references (Copilot CLI, Codex, Gemini CLI).

nodes.label: Codex Tool Mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps Task to spawn_agent/wait_agent/close_agent, TodoWrite to update_plan; requires multi_agent = true; includes environment detection and Codex App finishing.

nodes.label: Copilot CLI Tool Mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps Read/Write/Edit to view/create/edit, Task to task with agent_type, TodoWrite to sql todos table; adds async shell sessions and memory tools.

nodes.label: Gemini CLI Tool Mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps tools to read_file/write_file/replace/run_shell_command; subagents via @generalist syntax; includes parallel dispatch and memory tools.

nodes.label: Code Review Skill
nodes.rationale: INFERRED: code review is referenced as part of the superpowers workflow ecosystem (gemini-tools maps Task tool (superpowers:code-reviewer)).

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Skill Tool Mapping
nodes.rationale: Skills are written using Claude Code tool names (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Task, Skill); each non-Claude-Code platform maps them to its native equivalent (read_file, write_file, replace, run_shell_command, etc.).

nodes.label: Codex Tool Mapping Table
nodes.rationale: Codex maps skill tools to spawn_agent, wait_agent, close_agent, update_plan, and native file/shell tools; Task parallel calls become multiple spawn_agent calls.

nodes.label: Copilot CLI Tool Mapping Table
nodes.rationale: Copilot CLI maps Read/Write/Edit to view/create/edit, Bash to bash, Task to task with agent_type, TodoWrite to sql against a built-in todos table; WebSearch and PlanMode have no equivalent.

nodes.label: Gemini @generalist Subagent Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Gemini CLI dispatches subagents natively via the @ syntax; @generalist has access to all tools and follows the filled prompt template, so named agent types are replaced with @generalist plus the filled prompt.

nodes.label: Gemini Parallel Subagent Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Gemini CLI supports parallel subagent dispatch: independent tasks should be requested together in the same prompt while dependent tasks stay sequential.

nodes.label: Prompt Template Filling
nodes.rationale: Skills provide prompt templates with placeholders like {WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED}; all placeholders must be filled and the complete prompt passed as the message to @generalist.

nodes.label: Gemini-Only CLI Tools
nodes.rationale: Tools available in Gemini CLI with no Claude Code equivalent: list_directory, save_memory, ask_user, tracker_create_task, and enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode.

nodes.label: Codex Multi-Agent Config
nodes.rationale: spawn_agent, wait_agent, and close_agent require multi_agent = true under [features] in ~/.codex/config.toml; needed by dispatching-parallel-agents and subagent-driven-development skills.

nodes.label: Codex Git Environment Detection
nodes.rationale: Skills that create worktrees or finish branches detect environment with read-only git commands (rev-parse --git-dir/--git-common-dir, branch --show-current); GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON means already in a worktree, empty BRANCH means detached HEAD.

nodes.label: Codex App Finishing Workflow
nodes.rationale: When the sandbox blocks branch/push (detached HEAD in externally managed worktree), the agent commits work and the user finishes via the App's native 'Create branch' or 'Hand off to local' controls.

nodes.label: Copilot Async Shell Sessions
nodes.rationale: Copilot CLI supports persistent async shell sessions with no Claude Code equivalent: bash with async:true, write_bash, read_bash, stop_bash, list_bash.

nodes.label: Copilot Persistent Memory
nodes.rationale: store_memory persists facts about the codebase for future sessions, analogous to Gemini's save_memory writing to GEMINI.md.

nodes.label: Gemini save_memory
nodes.rationale: save_memory persists facts to GEMINI.md across sessions in Gemini CLI.

nodes.label: Gemini Plan Mode
nodes.rationale: enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode switch to read-only research mode before making changes.

nodes.label: Copilot-Only CLI Tools
nodes.rationale: Additional Copilot CLI tools: store_memory, report_intent, sql session database query, fetch_copilot_cli_documentation, and GitHub MCP tools (github-mcp-server-*).

nodes.label: Codex wait_agent Legacy Note
nodes.rationale: Codex builds before rust-v0.115.0 exposed spawned-agent waiting as wait; current Codex uses wait_agent, and wait now belongs to code-mode exec/wait.

nodes.label: Executing Plans Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt that requests implementation of an existing plan document at docs/superpowers/plans/2024-01-15-auth-system.md. Verifies the agent recognizes a 'execute existing plan' request and triggers the appropriate plan-execution skill.

nodes.label: Writing Plans Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt with an auth-system spec and multiple implementation steps (user model, auth routes, middleware, email service). Verifies the agent recognizes a multi-step feature request that should trigger the plan-writing skill before implementation.

nodes.label: Dispatching Parallel Agents Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt listing 4 independent test failures across different modules and asking to investigate all of them. Verifies the agent recognizes independent parallel work that should trigger parallel-agent dispatch.

nodes.label: Requesting Code Review Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt asking to review committed changes (commits abc123..def456) before merging to main. Verifies the agent triggers a code-review skill.

nodes.label: Systematic Debugging Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt with a failing test stack trace (TypeError in parser.ts) and a request to diagnose and fix. Verifies the agent triggers a systematic debugging skill.

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development Prompt (skill-triggering test)
nodes.rationale: Test prompt specifying requirements for an email-validation feature with explicit acceptance criteria. Verifies the agent recognizes a feature-implementation request that should trigger test-driven development (write tests first).
